header.name: Applied Fields and Waves
header.description: This course expands the basic understanding of fields and waves to its applied level. It will discuss the common high-frequency techniques for devices, circuits and systems. It introduces the concept of boundary conditions, different current sources and radiation concept. It then provides basic understanding of microwave network analysis techniques required for high-frequency circuit analysis. The course also includes few live demonstrations of characterizing radiating and guiding components using simulation tools and/or measurements.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to familiarize the importance of RF/ high-frequency engineering in modern-day electronics and real-world applications.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to evaluate unknown fields for simple problems using Maxwell's equations and boundary conditions.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to analyze microwave networks using S-parameters, solve impedance matching, signal integrity and related problems.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students acquire the ability to analyze, design, and simulate simple RF components.

lecture_topics: Introduction to RF engineering and applications
different RF problems related to modern circuits and systems
Boundary conditions between different medium interfaces
Concept of current sources and examples
simple solution techniques for unknown fields
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment:
Lab 1
Lab: DIY wire antenna and measurement techniques using VNA and SA

Lab 2
Lab: Measurement of S-parameters of transmission line with different loads

lecture_topics: Scattering parameters of power divider and directional coupler
weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment:
Lab 3
Lab: Measurement of S-parameters of a 3-port (power divider)/ 4-port (directional coupler) circuit
